questions.q: If a bicycle travels 10 kilometres in 2 hours, what is its speed?
questions.a: The speed is 5 km/h. A wrong answer (like 20 km/h) suggests the student multiplied distance and time instead of dividing, showing a misunderstanding of how "speed" represents a rate of change.

questions.q: Two cars travel the same distance. Car A takes 1 hour and Car B takes 2 hours. Which car is faster and why?
questions.a: Car A is faster. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks a larger time value means higher speed; they need to understand that speed is inversely related to time for a fixed distance.

questions.q: A bus travels 100 km in 2 hours. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.a: Speed = 100 km / 2 h = 50 km/h. A student who gets this wrong likely forgets to include the unit or confuses the order of division (Time/Distance).

questions.q: If you double the distance while keeping the time the same, what happens to your speed?
questions.a: The speed doubles. If a student says it stays the same, they are ignoring the relationship between the variables in the formula.

questions.q: Is it possible for a fast-moving object to have a lower speed value than a slow-moving object if the units are different?
questions.a: Yes, if the units are not the same (e.g., comparing 100 m/s to 5 km/h). Students often look only at the number and ignore the units, which is a critical error in scientific measurement.

questions.q: Design a simple experiment to prove that a marble rolling down a steep ramp is faster than one on a flat floor.
questions.a: The student should propose measuring the distance covered in a fixed time (e.g., 5 seconds) for both. A poor answer fails to keep one variable (time) constant, which is essential for a fair comparison.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Speed is the ______ an object travels in a specific amount of time.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you and your friend both start ______ from the school gate to the park.
What is Speed? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Speed is the distance an object travels in a specific amount of time.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Speed?
questions.a: Students often believe that "fast" means "long distance" regardless of time.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to calculate speed given distance and time and correctly identify which of two objects is faster based on their speed values.
